annotations.submission_query: SELECT c.name, SUM(i.quantity * i.unit_price) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY c.name HAVING total_spent > 500
annotations.human_reason: Oracle does not allow a select-list alias in HAVING; total_spent is not in scope there (ORA-00904).
annotations.llm_reason: The query computes the same per-customer total and applies the same threshold; using the aggregate alias total_spent in HAVING is semantically equivalent.

annotations.submission_query: SELECT c.name, SUM(i.quantity * p.unit_price) FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products p ON p.product_id = i.product_id GROUP BY c.name HAVING SUM(i.quantity * p.unit_price) > 500
annotations.human_reason: Uses the product's current list price instead of the price charged on the order line.
annotations.llm_reason: The query calculates spending with products.unit_price (the current list price) instead of order_items.unit_price (the price actually charged on the order). This can produce incorrect totals and include or exclude the wrong customers.
